title: Moving versus staying on a chord today
summary: With a good bass player Verrett moves chords; Lewis Nelson likes that, while older trumpet players did not.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: What I was going to say Harrison is you still do quite a bit of that type of playing don't you? Staying at one key? Yeah,

I do that sometimes, most of the time. Of course I'm not what bass player to have. Of course I'm not the other set and work the drummer and the bass player working. I'd stay like that. But if I got a good bass player I wouldn't stay there. Good bass player I'd move up. Instead of going for one chord you take one chord you play to D&D. Come on C. C. That's how you play now? Yeah, that's where we got a good bass player. Instead of staying on one card, see? Still staying on one card. I'll see you a long time. See, I won't do that. I'll move up. I'll see you a little bit. They're going to change. In that number you'll be playing instead of staying in one place.
It's prettier that way, but the old time trumpet players didn't think so.
They moved around and let you stay there.

What do you say? That's what you watch the players. See what you can see. You keep moving all the time. It keeps your fingers suple and everything. You keep your fingers in. You get a cramp in your fingers. And if you come there and your fingers ain't in yet, and you play more than one card, they never come in. And if you go to the crowd of cards, you can't. Well, they change up. They get mad at you. After the night, you're not awake anymore. I said, okay. Eventually, you see a couple of nights later. Come on, man, let's go. I think if it would, if you had a trumpet player or clarinet player or a trombone, it would.
If you were moving around, it would sort of throw him up a little bit, I guess.

Yeah, if he's not experiencing nothing. Yeah. See, like Lewis Nelson, he likes that. He likes what? He likes for you to move, yeah. Oh, he does?
